translate_en|mods/PixelStrikeIndicator/4: Animal Health Bars, Most Allowed
Off
Only When Hurt
Always

<RGB:1,1,1>The same, for animals. It is a
separate setting, so you can allow
one kind and turn off the other.

<RGB:1,1,1>Off: no bars on animals. Only When
Hurt: a bar appears after an animal
is hurt. Always: every animal near a
player has a bar.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Every animal has the same maximum
health, so the bar is correct the
first time a player looks. The
server does not have to send
anything for it.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Animals have no toughness bar. The
game does not give an animal a
toughness value the way it gives one
to a zombie.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start on Only When Hurt,
because a farm would otherwise show
a bar over every chicken.
How Far Health Bars Show, In Tiles

<RGB:1,1,1>How far away from a player a health
bar can still be drawn. This counts
for zombies and for animals.

<RGB:1,1,1>Each player also has a slider for
this, but theirs is a part of their
screen. This setting is the limit
for that slider. 60 is the furthest
the mod ever draws a bar, so 60
means no limit.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A wide screen shows more ground than
a small one, so the same player
setting is a different distance for
each player. This setting is in
tiles, so it is the same distance
for everybody.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Use a small number if you want
players to walk close to a zombie
before they can judge it. 4 is the
smallest, so a zombie standing next
to a player always has a bar.
Allow The Critical Hit Effect

<RGB:1,1,1>A critical hit is a strong hit that
the game gives at random. It gets a
bigger number in pale gold, a coral
star behind it, and the word
CRITICAL!! above.

<RGB:1,1,1>With this off, a critical hit looks
like a normal white hit and nothing
shows that it was special.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Melee weapons only. When a gun rolls
a critical hit the game turns it
into a shot to the head, which has
its own effect below.
Allow Damage A Player Deals

<RGB:1,1,1>The white number over anything a
player hits. This is the main thing
the mod draws.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A critical hit, a headshot and an
instant kill are the same number in
another colour with a word above it.
Turning this off removes those three
as well, even if they are allowed
further down.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off if you want the health
bars but no numbers.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It does not change the damage a
player takes, healing, fire on
zombies, the MISS word or the LEVEL
UP!! word. Each of those has a line
of its own.
Damage Multiplier, Most Allowed

<RGB:1,1,1>The number over a target is the
damage multiplied by this. It is
what makes a hit read as 150 instead
of 1.5.

<RGB:1,1,1>Each player has a slider for this,
and this setting is the limit for
that slider. They can choose less
than this, never more. 1000 is as
far as their slider goes, so 1000
means no limit. They all start at
100.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A strong axe hit is about 1.5
damage. At 100 it reads 150, at 10
it reads 15, and at 1 it reads 2.
The mod never draws less than 1, so
a low number here rounds hits of
different strengths to the same
digit.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Fire, falls, cars and healing are
counted on a scale of their own and
use a tenth of this. A door, a
window, a barricade, furniture and a
tree are not multiplied at all, so
this leaves them alone.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It only changes the number that is
drawn. Nothing hits any harder or
softer for it.
Allow Fire, Falls And Car Damage

<RGB:1,1,1>Damage from fire, from falling, and
from hitting or being hit by a car.
This is in addition to the damage
from being struck.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Only those four. Bleeding,
infection, hunger and thirst also
hurt a player, but none of them are
shown, because each one would print
a number every second until the
player is well again.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>This needs Allow Damage A Player
Takes to be on. With that off, none
of this is shown.
Allow The Headshot Effect

<RGB:1,1,1>When a bullet hits a zombie in the
head, the number is bigger and light
blue, a star opens behind it, and
the word HEADSHOT!! appears above.

<RGB:1,1,1>With this off, a headshot looks like
a normal white hit and only the size
of the number is different.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The game multiplies the damage of a
headshot by 3. That is why the
number is so much bigger than the
others, and why the zombie usually
dies.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Guns only. A melee weapon shows the
critical hit effect instead.
Allow Healing Numbers

<RGB:1,1,1>Health coming back shows as a green
number next to a player, in the same
way that damage shows in red.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The game sends no message when a
player heals, so the mod watches
their health instead. Healing is
slow and steady, so the mod adds it
up and shows one number instead of
many small ones.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>This is health coming back, not a
wound being treated. A bandage stops
the bleeding first, and the numbers
come over the hours after that.
Zombie Health Bars, Most Allowed
Off
Only When Hurt
Always

<RGB:1,1,1>The most that a player is allowed to
see. Each player then chooses for
themselves in Options, Mods, Pixel
Health Bars. They can choose less
than this, never more.

<RGB:1,1,1>Off: no bars on zombies. Only When
Hurt: a bar appears after a zombie
takes its first hit. Always: every
zombie near a player has a bar.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The bar shows how much health that
one zombie has left. Zombies are not
all equally strong, so a full bar
does not mean a strong zombie.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Off also removes the toughness bar
and the right mouse button check,
because both are drawn on the health
bar.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Animals have their own setting, on
the next line.
Allow The Health Percentage

<RGB:1,1,1>A small number next to the bar. It
counts down from 100 to 0 as the
zombie loses health.

<RGB:1,1,1>It says the same thing as the bar,
but as an exact number instead of a
length to judge by eye.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off if you want players to
read the bar only.
Allow The Right Mouse Button Check

<RGB:1,1,1>A player holds the right mouse
button and points at a zombie. That
zombie shows its bar, even if nobody
has hit it yet.

<RGB:1,1,1>It is a way to check one zombie
without keeping every bar on the
screen all the time.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a player only sees
the bars that their own setting
gives them.
Allow The Instant Kill Effect

<RGB:1,1,1>A knife pushed into a zombie's jaw
kills it at once, whatever health it
had left. That kill gets its own
number, a star behind it, and the
word INSTAKILL!! above.

<RGB:1,1,1>With this off, the kill looks like a
normal white hit and nothing shows
that it was special.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Melee weapons and knives only. The
game does it when a zombie stands
close in front of a player, and it
is the same moment that can leave
the knife stuck in the zombie.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>It is stronger than a critical hit.
If one hit is both, the mod shows
this word and not the other one,
because this one is rarer.
Allow The Level Up Banner

<RGB:1,1,1>The words LEVEL UP!! appear over a
player, with wings behind them, when
one of their skills reaches a new
level.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It does not say which skill. The
skill panel already does, and a
skill name would have to be drawn in
a game font instead of the font the
player chose.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and only the skill panel
and the sound the game already plays
tell the player.
Allow The Miss Banner

<RGB:1,1,1>When a player swings a melee weapon
and hits nothing, the white word
MISS appears where they stand.

<RGB:1,1,1>It only appears when a zombie was
close enough to be the target, so
swinging at empty space stays quiet.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Melee weapons only. A gun cannot
miss in this game: a shot either
hits something or is never fired, so
a gun can never show this.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a missed swing shows
nothing.
Allow Damage On Doors And Trees

<RGB:1,1,1>A number over a door, a window, a
barricade, a piece of furniture or a
tree when a player hits it, where a
number over a zombie would be.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It is the health the swing took off
that door, not the damage a zombie
would have taken, because a door is
counted on a scale of its own. The
damage multiplier does not touch it.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>A multiplayer client is never told
what a swing took off a door,
because the server settles that on
its own, so these numbers are for
single player and for the host.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Players start with this off.
Breaking into a house is a long run
of swings and it is a lot of
numbers.
Allow Bars Through Walls

<RGB:1,1,1>A health bar over a zombie that a
player cannot see: behind a wall,
inside a dark room, or anywhere
their character has no view of.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The mod asks the game the same
question the game asks itself before
it draws a zombie. When the answer
is no the zombie is not drawn
either, so the bar would be floating
over a wall.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to make this impossible
for everyone. A player who hurt a
zombie then loses its bar as soon as
that zombie is out of sight, and
gets it back when they see it again.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start with this off, so
nobody sees through a wall unless
they ask for it.
Allow Damage A Player Takes

<RGB:1,1,1>The red number next to a player when
something hurts them. It flies to
the left, and the damage they deal
flies to the right, so the two are
easy to tell apart.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a player only sees
the damage they deal. This also
removes fire, falls and car damage.
Share Zombie Health Between Players

<RGB:1,1,1>Every player sees the same health
bar and the same toughness bar for a
zombie, because the server tells
them how much health that zombie
started with.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A player's game can see how much
health a zombie has now, but it can
never ask how much it had at the
start. Without this, a zombie that
another player already fought looks
unhurt to everyone who meets it
later, and its toughness bar looks
short.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to save network traffic.
Each player then uses the most
health they have seen themselves,
and two players can see different
bars on the same zombie.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It costs one small request per
player every few seconds, and only
while that player has zombies close
enough to have a bar.
Allow The Toughness Bar

<RGB:1,1,1>A second, thinner bar under the
health bar. It does not move when a
zombie is hurt.

<RGB:1,1,1>It shows how much damage that zombie
can take in total. A long bar means
a zombie that needs many more hits
than a short one, so a player can
decide before they attack.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>This only tells a player something
when Toughness, under Zombie Lore,
is set to Random. That is what
Apocalypse uses. With the other
settings every zombie is nearly the
same and every bar looks alike.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off if you want the strength
of a zombie to be a surprise.
Allow Fire Damage On Zombies

<RGB:1,1,1>A burning zombie shows an orange
number for the damage the fire is
doing. A player can then see whether
the fire is working or only making
light.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The game sends no message when fire
hurts a zombie, so the mod finds it
by watching the health of nearby
zombies. It therefore only covers
zombies close enough to have a bar,
and only while they burn.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a player has to
judge the fire with their eyes.

Critical Hit Star
Critical Hit Star Colour
The colour of the star behind a critical hit. It is a separate setting, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Turn it off to keep the pale gold number and the word without the star, which is the loudest part.
Critical Hit Number Colour
The colour of the number and of the word CRITICAL!!. Any colour works, because the mod draws them in grey and then paints them.
Critical Hit Effect

A critical hit is a strong hit that the game gives at random. It gets a bigger number in pale gold, a star, and the word CRITICAL!! above. Melee weapons only: a gun turns its critical hits into headshots. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Critical Hit Word
The word CRITICAL!! above the number. Turn it off to keep the bigger pale gold number and the star without the word. The number then sits on the path any other number takes.
Show Damage You Deal
The white number over anything you hit. This is the main thing the mod draws. Turning it off keeps the health bars and everything else. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Show Fire, Falls And Car Damage
Damage from fire, from falling and from cars, not only from being hit. You need Show Damage You Take for this. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Zombie Fire Colour
The colour of the number on a burning zombie. You need Show Fire Damage On Zombies turned on to see it at all.
Seconds Between Fire Numbers, Longer Is Bigger
Headshot Star
Headshot Star Colour
The colour of the star behind a headshot. It is a separate setting, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Turn it off to keep the light blue number and the word without the star, which is the loudest part.
Headshot Number Colour
The colour of the number and of the word HEADSHOT!!. Any colour works, because the mod draws them in grey and then paints them.
Headshot Effect
A bullet in a zombie's head gets a bigger light blue number, a star, and the word HEADSHOT!! above. The game multiplies that damage by 3, so it usually kills. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Headshot Word
The word HEADSHOT!! above the number. Turn it off to keep the bigger light blue number and the star without the word.
Healing Star
Healing Star Colour
The colour of the star behind a healing number. You need Healing Star turned on to see it at all.
This starts off. Healing happens slowly over time, not in one moment, so a star does not fit it.
Healing Number Colour
The colour of the number. Any colour works, because the mod draws it in grey and then paints it.
Show Healing
Health coming back, as a green number next to you. Healing is slow, so the mod adds it up and shows one number instead of many small ones. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Zombie Health Bars
Off
Only When Hurt
Always
Show Health Percentage
How much health a zombie has left, counting down from 100 to 0 next to the bar, in the same font as the damage numbers. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Damage You Deal Colour
The colour of the number over anything you hit. This is the one you see most, so it starts white, which reads over any ground.
Damage You Take Colour
The colour of the number next to you when something hurts you. Fire, falls and cars use this one too.
Show A Bar With Right Mouse Held
Hold the right mouse button and point at a zombie to see its bar, even one nobody has hit yet. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Instant Kill Star
Instant Kill Star Colour
The colour of the star behind an instant kill. It is a separate setting, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Turn it off to keep the number and the word without the star, which is the loudest part.
Instant Kill Number Colour
The colour of the number and of the word INSTAKILL!!. Any colour works, because the mod draws them in grey and then paints them.
Instant Kill Effect

A knife pushed into a zombie's jaw kills it at once. That kill gets a bigger number in bone white, a star, and the word INSTAKILL!! above. If one hit is both, you see this instead of a critical hit. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Instant Kill Word
The word INSTAKILL!! above the number. Turn it off to keep the bigger bone white number and the star without the word.
Level Up Wings
Level Up Wings Colour
The colour of the wings behind the words. It is a separate setting, so they can sit under the words instead of matching them.
The pair of wings that opens behind the words. Turn them off to keep only the words. Every other effect uses a star, and this one uses wings.
Level Up Banner Colour
The colour of the words LEVEL UP!!. They have no number under them, so this is their whole colour.
Level Up Banner
The words LEVEL UP!! appear over you when one of your skills reaches a new level. It does not say which skill. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Show The Health Just Lost
The health a zombie just lost stays on the bar as a white part for a moment, then slides down to the health that is left.
Miss Star
Miss Star Colour
The colour of the star behind the word MISS. You need Miss Star turned on to see it at all.
This starts off. The star marks something good, and a miss is not good news.
Miss Banner Colour
The colour of the word MISS. It has no number under it, so this is its whole colour.
Miss Banner
When you swing a melee weapon and hit nothing, the white word MISS appears where you stand. It only appears when a zombie was close enough to be the target. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Doors And Trees Colour
The colour of that number. It starts a pale steel blue, so a door reads apart from the white of a zombie at a glance.
Show Damage On Doors And Trees

A number when you hit a door, a window, a barricade, furniture or a tree. It is the health the swing took off, which is counted on a scale of its own, so it does not read like the number over a zombie and the damage multiplier leaves it alone. This starts off, because breaking into a house is a lot of swings. On a multiplayer client it stays quiet, because the server settles a door and never says by how much. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Your Own Settings, Inside The Server's Limits
Put This Page Back To Its Defaults
Sets every setting on this page back to the value it had when you installed the mod. The other page does not change.
Damage Multiplier, 100 Shows An Axe Hit As 150
Show Bars Through Walls

A bar over a zombie you cannot see, for example behind a wall or in a dark room. This starts off, so a bar only appears while your character can see that zombie. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Blocks In The Health Bar, 0 For One Plain Bar
Show Damage You Take
The red number next to you when something hurts you. It flies to the left, and the damage you deal flies to the right. A server can turn this off for everyone.

Height Of The Toughness Bar, 100 Is Normal
Show How Tough A Zombie Is

A thinner bar under the health bar. It shows how much damage that zombie can take in total, not how hurt it is now. It only tells you something when Toughness is set to Random. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Mark A Normal Zombie
One pale line across the toughness bar, at the health of an ordinary zombie. If the bar is longer than the line, this zombie is tougher than normal. Shorter means weaker.
Show Fire Damage On Zombies

A burning zombie shows an orange number for the damage the fire does. Fire takes the same amount from every zombie, so the number looks the same on all of them. A server can turn this off for everyone.
